children.text: A small island with a coastline of only about
64 km

, dotted with several volcanic cones — "the island born of fire." You can cover White Island's sandbar, the Sunken Cemetery, hot and cold springs, and waterfalls in a day or two, and the friendly locals make it one of the most relaxing island getaways in Mindanao.
Camiguin is a small volcanic island in the Bohol Sea north of Mindanao, and it's the second-smallest province in the Philippines. The coastal road that circles the island runs only about
64 km

, yet this small stretch of land is dotted with several large and small volcanic cones, earning it the nickname "Island Born of Fire." At the island's center stand the active volcano Hibok-Hibok and Mount Timpoong, rising to about
, and this area is protected as the Mount Timpoong–Hibok-Hibok Natural Monument.
Camiguin's scenery is a direct record of its volcanic history. In

, a new volcano (Old Volcano, or Vulcan Point) rose on the island's western side, and the village of that time sank beneath the sea — today marked by the giant cross that stands over the water, known as the Sunken Cemetery. In

, Hibok-Hibok erupted, causing major damage and hundreds of deaths. This volcanic landscape is also why hot springs, cold springs, and carbonated springs bubble up all over the island, and streams flowing down the mountains form waterfalls large and small.

Off the island's northern coast lies White Island, a white sandbar that changes shape with the tide; standing on the sand and looking up at Hibok-Hibok has become the classic image of Camiguin. Mantigue Island to the east is a marine protected area, good for snorkeling and diving.

Camiguin's people are friendly and the island is generally safe, so it carries little of the worry first-time Mindanao visitors might feel. You can circle the island in a day by motorbike or multicab (a small pickup taxi) along the coastal road, which suits family travelers, couples, and motorbike riders alike. During the Lanzones Festival in
October
, the whole island fills with the sweet scent of the local lanzones fruit.
An uninhabited sandbar reached by bangka in about
10–15 minutes
from Agoho or Yumbing beach in Mambajao. There's no shade at all, so it's best to go in the early morning while the sun is still gentle (
); the classic shot has Hibok-Hibok volcano rising behind the sandbar.
The large cross off the Catarman coast marks an old cemetery that was submerged by the
eruption. You can take a bangka right up to the cross or snorkel nearby, and the view at sunset is especially beautiful.
A path along the slope of Vulcan Point lined with statues depicting the 14 Stations of the Cross. A climb of about
30–40 minutes
brings you to a view over the Sunken Cemetery and the sea, and the walkway draws many pilgrims during Holy Week.
A slender waterfall that drops straight down from a height of about
, with a cold pool for swimming below. It's close to Mambajao town, making it easy to fit into a half-day itinerary.

blocks.title: Comparing the hot and cold springs

children.text: Ardent Hot Spring's volcanically warmed water flows through tiered pools, while Sto. Niño Cold Spring in Catarman stays cold enough to feel chilly even in the height of summer. Visiting both in the same day lets you feel Camiguin's volcanic geology firsthand.

A small island off Mahinog on the east coast, protected as a marine sanctuary with good chances of seeing coral and sea turtles. Its white sand and forest also make it a pleasant half-day picnic spot.

blocks.title: Guiwanon Church ruins and giant clam sanctuary

children.text: The Guiwanon church ruins in Bonbon village are the remaining walls of a coral-stone church destroyed in the
eruption. In Ginsiliban Catan-agan in the island's south, there's a sanctuary where you can see giant clams up close.
Camiguin pastel is a soft bread filled with sweet ube or custard cream, sold as a souvenir across the Philippines. From September to
October
, the island's signature lanzones fruit is in season, and picking up a bag at the market is one of the pleasures of the trip.

Visit Ardent Hot Spring and Katibawasan Falls.
Stroll through Mambajao town, then watch the sunset from your accommodation on Agoho or Yumbing beach.
Swim and take photos in the morning at White Island's sandbar.
Head west to visit the Walkway to the Old Volcano, the Sunken Cemetery, and the Guiwanon church ruins.
Have a seafood lunch at a coastal restaurant in Bonbon or Catarman.
Visit Sto. Niño Cold Spring, Tuasan Falls, and the soda water pool in turn.
Finish the loop by passing the giant clam sanctuary in Ginsiliban in the south and returning along the east coast road.
Take a bangka from Mahinog to Mantigue Island for snorkeling.
Buy pastel, lanzones, and other souvenirs, then head to the airport or Benoni port.
The fastest option is a direct flight from Cebu to Camiguin Airport (CGM, Mambajao). Cebgo operates about seven flights a week, with a flight time of about
50 minutes
. From Manila, you can connect through Cebu, or fly directly to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) in Cagayan de Oro (about
1 hour 30 minutes
, one-way around
) and continue by land and sea. Camiguin Airport flights have limited seats and sell out early in peak season, so book ahead.
From Laguindingan Airport, an airport shuttle van to the Agora bus terminal in Cagayan de Oro city takes about
1 hour
(around
). From Agora terminal, a bus to Balingoan takes about
1 hour 30 minutes–2 hours
, at a fare of about
. You can also charter a van from the airport straight to Balingoan.
The ferry from Balingoan Port to Benoni Port in Camiguin takes about
1 hour
and costs about
one way. Several operators take turns running from around
to around
4–5 PM
, and a separate port terminal fee of about
is added. Boats thin out in the late afternoon, so the safest plan is to arrive at Balingoan by
at the latest. There is also a RoRo ferry about once a day between Jagna in Bohol and Balbagon Port in Mambajao, taking about
4 hours 30 minutes
and costing about
one way.
From Benoni port to Mambajao takes about
30 minutes
by jeepney or multicab. To circle the island, choose between chartering a multicab (about
a day, for 4–6 people), renting a motorbike (about
a day), or riding tricycles for shorter stretches. An international driving permit and a helmet are required to rent a motorbike.
Camiguin gets fairly even rainfall year-round, but
March
through
June
is the driest stretch and the sea is calmest, making it the best time to visit White Island and Mantigue Island. From
November
to
January
, the northeast monsoon brings frequent rain, and bangkas to White Island sometimes can't run because of the waves.
Typhoons mostly pass north of Camiguin, but in some years a late typhoon around
December
crosses northern Mindanao, so it's worth checking the forecast during that period. The island's best-known event is the Lanzones Festival, held around the third week of
October

each year in Mambajao, featuring a street parade in lanzones-themed costumes and a fruit market. During the festival and Holy Week, accommodation fills up fast, so it's best to book more than a month ahead.

Most accommodation is clustered around Agoho, Yumbing, and Baylao beaches near Mambajao in the island's north. This area is close to the White Island pier and has plenty of restaurants, making it the most convenient base for first-time visitors. Simple guesthouses run about
a night, and beach resorts about
, with a few upscale pool-villa resorts as well. For a quieter atmosphere, accommodation on the island's southwest coast around Catarman and Bonbon is also good.

Fresh seafood and fruit anchor the food scene. Grilled fish and kinilaw are common at coastal restaurants, and squid adobo is popular too, while fresh fruit is cheap in the market and roadside stalls during lanzones season. Camiguin pastel has been the island's signature snack since the
, and Vjandep in Mambajao town is the most famous original shop. Small cafes serving coffee grown on the island, along with mango and coconut desserts, are also on the rise.
Mambajao town has a few ATMs, but breakdowns and cash shortages are common. It's safer to withdraw plenty of cash in Cagayan de Oro or Cebu beforehand.
The sand at White Island gets hot at midday and there's no shade. Visit between
6 and 9 a.m.
and bring a hat, umbrella, and plenty of water.
The Balingoan ferry boards on a first-come basis, so waits can be long on peak-season weekends. Aiming for the first early-morning boat gives you more breathing room.
The island's loop road is well paved but has sharp curves and climbs on some stretches. If you're new to riding a motorbike, a multicab tour is the safer choice.
Each attraction collects its own entrance fee in cash, so it's worth carrying plenty of small bills —
, and
notes.
Climbing Hibok-Hibok requires permission from the protected-area management office and a registered guide. Check availability and fees in advance at the Mambajao tourism office.
Sunset at the Sunken Cemetery is at its most beautiful around
. Scheduling your western-side visits for the afternoon lines up naturally with this.
Phone signal reaches most of the island well, but it can be weak near mountain waterfalls.
If you plan to continue to Bohol, the Balbagon–Jagna ferry runs only once a day (leaving Balbagon around
), so check the port or shipping company page the day before to confirm it's running. In
, ferry fares may be higher than posted fares because of fuel surcharges.

Hibok-Hibok remains an active volcano. If the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) raises its alert level, climbing and access to the surrounding area may be restricted, so check the latest bulletins.
The waters around White Island and Mantigue Island have stretches of fast current. It's safer not to swim out alone toward the open sea.
Don't touch or step on coral or shells at Mantigue Island or the giant clam sanctuary. Violating protected-area rules can carry a fine.
Rocks around the waterfalls are very slippery from moss. Wear water shoes and avoid climbing over rocks right after rain.
Wearing a helmet is mandatory when renting a motorbike, and many stretches have no streetlights at night, so it's safer to avoid riding after dark.
The last ferry from Balingoan to Benoni runs around
. If you leave Cagayan de Oro too late, you may have to spend the night in Balingoan, so leave plenty of time for the journey.
About
2 hours
by bus from Balingoan port, the gateway city of northern Mindanao, known for white-water rafting and a lively night market.
About
1 hour 30 minutes
by car from Cagayan de Oro, offering ziplines through pine forest and cool highland air.
About
4 hours 30 minutes
by ferry from Balbagon Port to Jagna, an island famous for the Chocolate Hills and tarsiers.
About
3–4 hours
by car via Cagayan de Oro to Iligan, one of the Philippines' great waterfalls, now open to advance-registered visitors only.
